title: Apply the review-3 prose, lifecycle-rendering and visual deltas
source_handoff: third review round, the items that fall outside the cache chapter and the registry
acceptance_criteria: The placement ladder no longer calls the cache 'the fastest read' or 'the only step that adds a consistency contract': copy-out can be the lowest-latency hot read for the measured workload and adds a freshness and failure-domain contract because it crosses the transaction boundary, while indexes, rollups and rolldowns carry maintenance correctness of their own

Partially superseded cards render the lifecycle explicitly: moved-to successor claims with their ids, what is still open in the claim, and the statement labelled as unchanged from its source registry; the statement itself stays verbatim

Repeat citations of a claim render a one-line capsule carrying the claim id, strength, the limit line and a pointer to the full card; the first citation keeps the full card and no limit line is dropped
A lease-versus-fence figure is authored as a book-owned source with form and evidence-status labels, an adjacent text equivalent, no embedded number and a manifest entry
The page-3 evidence legend takes its gap kinds from the registry enum rather than restating them by hand
Chapter 6's 'replication turns a write into a consensus write' is scoped to the measured YugabyteDB RF=3 topology
Chapter 17's closed-loop tail 'is a floor, not an SLO' becomes a statement that closed-loop load can understate fixed-rate behaviour and must not be read as an SLO prediction
validation: every repeat citation still shows a limit line
